title: TypeScript SDK: consumer handshake semantics + examples for AsyncIterator <-> Web Streams
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Design and deliver a concise spec + examples that define deterministic handshake semantics between the TypeScript SDK's AsyncIterator surface and the Web Streams (ReadableStream) surface. Goal: remove ambiguity for library consumers about cancellation, backpressure, error propagation, and resumable consumption across network transient failures. The artifact should include a spec, representative code examples (dual-consumer patterns, progressive hydration, graceful fallback to chunked responses), test plan, and a small reference implementation in the SDK under an experimental flag.
acceptance_criteria: A one-page spec that explicitly maps: AsyncIterator.next()/return()/throw() to ReadableStream controller signals (enqueue/close/error/cancel)

Examples demonstrating: A) single consumer AsyncIterator; B) single consumer ReadableStream; C) dual-consumer handoff (handover from ReadableStream to AsyncIterator and vice-versa) with no message duplication or loss
Clear rules for backpressure: how SDK signals pause/resume to the server, and how underlying fetch/readable strategies map to kernel batching policies
Cancellation semantics documented: consumer-initiated abort propagation, server-initiated shutdown, and how the SDK exposes cancel tokens and graceful drain hooks
Integration tests that simulate network interruption and verify resume semantics for resumable handoffs (not full replay) included in CI
Examples and tests use only stable TS SDK APIs or behind experimental flag and are linked from README
Performance smoke: microbenchmark showing no more than 5% latency regression for non-handshake paths when feature is enabled (relative to baseline)

testing_plan: Unit tests for adapter primitives (enqueue/close/error/cancel mapping), integration tests that run headless Node fetch with controlled packet-loss shim, E2E that validates dual-consumer handoff in example app (examples/stream-handoff). Add CI job 'ts-stream-handshake' to run flaky-network matrix nightly.
implementation_notes: Reference implementation lives in sdk/packages/ts/src/stream/handshake-adapter.ts behind REDWOOD_EXPERIMENTAL_STREAM_HANDSHAKE. Key primitives: HandshakeToken (uuid string), fragment markers for idempotency, gracefulDrain(timeoutMs) that returns a promise resolved when server ack or timeout. Avoids circular dependency on runtime by using the public fetch wrapper. Benchmark harness: tools/bench/stream-handshake.js
migration_guide: For customers with existing custom ReadableStream adapters: use Adapter.toAsyncIterator(adapter) which will wrap with a pass-through idempotency marker. Recommend toggling feature and validating in staging. See docs link: https://docs.redwood.ai/sdk/ts/streaming-handshake-examples.md
notes_for_release: Ship behind experimental flag in sdk-2025.03. Include a short note in release changelog advising customers to opt-in and providing link to examples and known limitations (no resume after server restart; resume only across transient network errors).
